title: AI consulting services: what you should get
description: What AI consulting should deliver, how to test a firm's claims on your own documents, and when to hire help versus build an in-house team.
summary: Good AI consulting turns one business problem into a tested, working system. Before anything is built, the right AI model is chosen by testing it on your own documents, not on a demo or a public leaderboard.

example.input: A mid-sized insurer wants AI to read incoming claim files and route them.
example.output: A test of several AI models on 50 of the insurer's own claim files, the cost per file for each, a working pilot with the winner, and a plan to keep it accurate as models change.

howToTest: Ask the firm to test its approach on 20 to 50 of your own documents before you sign for a full build.
Agree the right answers first with your own team, so the result is graded against your standard, not theirs.
Ask for cost per correct answer, not price per token: the cheapest-looking model is not always the cheapest to run.
Ask for a client reference where the system has run for at least six months.

buyVsBuild.buy: Hire a firm when you need one system working this quarter and have no AI engineers. Pay for a fixed scope with a test you can check.
buyVsBuild.build: Hire in-house when AI is core to what you sell and you will run many systems. Expect months to hire and a higher fixed cost.

watchOuts: Firms that resell one software vendor's product and call it a recommendation.
Demos on clean sample data that never meet your real documents.
No answer key: without agreed right answers, nobody can show the system works.
